result:
The critical exponent is $p = 3/2$. I did not verify this by derivation. It is my best recollection of the sharp threshold reported for this setting, which I could not check against the source.

The system is the stationary pressureless Euler system in $\mathbb{R}^2$: $\operatorname{div}(\rho u) = 0$ and $\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u) = 0$. The differential inclusion is written in terms of the unknowns $(\rho, m)$ with $m = \rho u$. The claim is that sequences bounded in $L^{p-\epsilon}$ can be approximated by convex-integration flexibility, while sequences bounded in $L^{p+\epsilon}$ are rigid. The threshold $3/2$ is the exponent at which the quadratic term $|m|^2/\rho$ becomes integrable enough to control the compensated-compactness argument in two dimensions.

ANSWER: 3/2
